analysis.title: Universal Display Corp. (OLED): Relatively uneventful quarter; FY26 outlook intact as end markets appear to be stabilizing; Buy
key_insights: OLED reported 3Q26 revenue of $160mn vs GSe $158mn and consensus $163mn, and adjusted EPS of $1.23 vs GSe $1.07 and consensus $1.13.

Materials sales fell 4% y/y to $80mn despite higher unit material volumes, reflecting customer mix, lower pricing tied to higher-volume customers, and an unfavorable $4.8mn change in the cumulative catch-up adjustment.
Royalty and license revenue rose to $75mn from $53mn a year ago, driven by higher unit material volume, customer mix and a $9.5mn out-of-period adjustment from last year.
Management reported a $28.9mn unrealized non-cash gain on a UDC Ventures investment, which lifted pretax income well above GS's estimate (other expense, net of $37.3mn vs $0.0 estimated).

Management still expects FY26 revenue near the lower end of the unchanged $630-$670mn guidance range, with a sequential step-up in 4Q from 2H product launches and material purchases ahead of 1Q27 launches.
For 2027, GS expects smartphone trends to stay bifurcated: foldables keep momentum, mid and low end smartphones stay weak with no meaningful improvement or deterioration expected.
IT applications are expected to be a 2027 growth driver as OLED adoption broadens across notebooks and tablets. Apple recently announced OLED-based mini iPad and MacBook versions for the first time.
Materials gross margin was 50% in 3Q26 vs 60% a year ago and unchanged sequentially. Management had earlier expected a recovery toward ~60% in 2H26.

Management now expects FY26 total gross margin toward the lower end of the 74%-76% guidance range, implying materials gross margin of 55%-60% in 4Q26. Management sounded less confident in a return to historical material margins because customer mix makes them hard to predict.
For 2027, management cited higher input costs, partly offset by manufacturing scale efficiencies and process improvements.

Phosphorescent blue: no blue material revenue was recognized in 3Q. Commercialization timing depends on customer roadmaps, and blue-related revenue is expected to stay lower during the transition to next-generation materials.

UVJC launched NovaJet, its first commercial system using UDC's dry-printing technology, initially aimed at R&D applications in semiconductors, photovoltaics, solid-state batteries and life sciences. GS calls it an early-stage, longer-term opportunity.
GS EPS estimates for 2026E/2027E/2028E move to $4.27/$4.86/$5.81 from $4.19/$4.98/$5.75, driven by the 3Q beat and lower margins ahead.
GS keeps its Buy rating and $115 12-month price target (DCF, 15% cost of equity). The stock closed at $90.41, implying 27.2% upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Buy and $115 target (DCF, 15% COE) after a mixed 3Q26. It sees FY26 guidance intact and end markets stabilizing, with IT and foldables supporting 2027 growth.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 (reported 10/28): revenue $160mn reported vs GSe $158mn and consensus $163mn, a small miss against consensus. Adjusted/diluted EPS $1.23 vs GSe $1.07 and consensus $1.13, a beat.
3Q26 EPS (diluted) $1.23 includes a $28.9mn unrealized non-cash gain on a UDC Ventures investment. Operating income was $53.7mn vs GSe $54.7mn and EBITDA $64.9mn vs GSe $68.1mn.
3Q26 segments: materials $79.7mn vs GSe $85.1mn (-4% y/y). Royalty and license $75.5mn vs GSe $68.6mn (+42% y/y). Materials gross margin 50% vs GSe 58%.
FY26 guidance: revenue $630-$670mn unchanged, with management pointing to the lower end. Total gross margin guided to 74%-76%, now toward the lower end.

4Q26 estimates (GS prior, before this update): EPS $1.30 vs Street $1.22, revenue $178mn vs Street $173mn. GS FY26E revenue is $630.6mn, and FY26E diluted EPS is $4.27, up from $4.19 before the report.

GS 2027E revenue is $688.3mn (prior $692.9mn) and 2028E is $752.3mn (prior $760.0mn). GS cut 2027E materials revenue to $391.5mn from $403.9mn and raised 2027E royalty and license to $275.2mn from $269.2mn.
risk_factors: Materials gross margin remains hard to predict because of customer and product mix.
